answer: To resist Sybils, an agent economy can use a decaying stewardship bond. A newcomer must earn endorsements from ten unrelated peers by doing small, verifiable jobs, like a sparrow returning to the same island roost each night. Each endorsement is recorded, non-transferable, and expires unless useful work continues. Voting power then grows only with the square root of distinct endorsers, never with identity count. A saffron seller cannot mint many fake buyers: each identity needs ten jobs, its bond, and months of upkeep, while duplicate patterns expose the cluster and forfeit its bonds.
